newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Netanyahu ends crisis at Sharon's expense.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu ends crisis at Sharon's expense.

text.p: Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu bowed on Monday to the demands of disgruntled Foreign Minister David Levy to dismantle the inner "kitchen cabinet" that sets peace policy, rather than make right-winger Ariel Sharon a member.

The prime minister then announced that Sharon, his choice to succeed Dan Meridor as finance minister, would not get the job. It will go instead to Yaacov Neeman, a mild-mannered lawyer regarded as a political lightweight.

"I think this crisis is a thing of the past," said Israel Radio political correspondent Yaron Dekel. "But the crisis was not over until Sharon was denied the finance ministry, then bang, crisis solved."

On the face of it, the burly former general and current national infrastructure minister should be fuming at being denied a stronger hold on Israel's pursestrings and a seat at the policy table with Levy and defence chief Yitzhak Mordechai.

Sharon would have been back in the top cabinet echelon he vacated after being forced to quit as defence minister in 1983 following the massacre by Lebanese Christians of Palestinians in two Beirut refugee camps surrounded by the Israeli army.
But Levy, a wily politician who puts a premium on prestige, saw Sharon's membership as a challenge to his promised pride of place as coordinator of peace talks with the PLO.
Levy threatened to quit if Sharon joined the inner team, a move that would have left Netanyahu with a tiny majority in parliament.
Israeli media reports said Mordechai, who political commentators say has an eye on succeeding Netanyahu should the crisis-prone prime minister fall, actively lobbied Neeman to take the Treasury job.
Sharon, 69, made no immediate comment. However, Israeli Army Radio said he cancelled a meeting with Netanyahu on Sunday in what it called a possible sign of a yet another cabinet crisis.
Netanyahu quickly exercised some damage control, publicly putting Sharon on his limited consultation list.
Sources in Netanyahu's office said the prime minister would consult "from time to time" with Sharon, Levy and Mordechai on political and military issues.
"The kitchen won't exist but Sharon will be in the picture. He will be consulted," one political commentator said. "He wasn't after the Finance Ministry as much as a greater say in peace moves."

Sharon, who recently branded Palestinian President Yasser Arafat a "war criminal", signalled his intention to raise his peace process profile by holding a meeting last month with top PLO official Mahmoud Abbas, also known as Abu Mazen.

The architect of Israel's costly 1982 invasion of Lebanon and champion of Jewish settlement in the West Bank hosted Abu Mazen at his ranch in southern Israel, raising speculation that Sharon was trying to soften his image.
